name: Pleiades
tagline: The Seven Sisters — a jewel-box of young blue stars wrapped in reflection nebulosity.
history: The Pleiades are the sky's most famous open cluster — a handful of brilliant blue giants visible to the naked eye, sitting atop hundreds of fainter siblings all born from the same molecular cloud. Long-exposure images reveal the stars wading through dusty reflection nebulae — unrelated material the cluster is currently passing through, not its birth cloud. Recorded since antiquity (Homer, the Bible, Māori Matariki), it remains the benchmark for how star clusters age and disperse.
